step.name: Step 1: Secure the Scene and Call for Help.
step.text: First, move to a safe spot if possible and check for injuries. Call 911 for emergencies and non-emergencies alike to ensure a police report is filed. Don't assume the other driver will do it, and don't skip this step even for seemingly minor bumps, as an official report is crucial.

step.name: Step 2: Exchange Information with the Other Driver.
step.text: Get their full name, contact information, insurance company and policy number, and vehicle make, model, and license plate number. Be polite but firm, and stick to the facts about exchanging details without discussing fault or details of the accident itself.

step.name: Step 3: Photograph Everything.
step.text: Use your phone to take pictures of the damage to both vehicles from multiple angles. Get shots of the entire scene, including road conditions, traffic signals, and any relevant landmarks. Don't forget to photograph any visible injuries you or your passengers may have sustained. More photos are always better than too few.

step.name: Step 4: Collect Witness Information.
step.text: If anyone saw the accident, politely ask for their name and contact information. Witness statements can provide objective accounts that significantly strengthen your claim, especially if there's a dispute over who was at fault.

step.name: Step 5: Seek Medical Attention Promptly.
step.text: Even if you feel fine, see a doctor within 24-48 hours. Many injuries, particularly soft tissue injuries from rear-end impacts, might not present symptoms immediately. Early medical documentation directly links your injuries to the accident and is vital for your claim.

step.name: Step 6: Keep a Detailed Accident Journal.
step.text: Start a journal where you record everything you remember about the accident itself, your daily pain levels, medical appointments, medications, and how your injuries are impacting your life. This ongoing record helps paint a clear picture of your experience and recovery.

step.name: Step 7: Contact a Knowledgeable Attorney.
step.text: Once you've done the initial steps, reach out to an experienced rear-end collision lawyer. They can review your documentation, advise you on the next steps, and handle communications with insurance companies. Brett Peterson, for example, makes sure you have a clear strategy and don't miss any critical deadlines.
